clue.text: Blooming accompaniment for cold veg?

indicators.note: the blooming word goes alongside the word for cold, following it

parts.note: a chill is a cold, as in catching a chill
a flower that is blooming is said to be out

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which flowery garnish should go with a plate of chilled vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'veg' looks like vegetables but is the slang verb, as in to veg in front of the TV. 'accompaniment for' places the word for blooming beside the word for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to veg is to relax and do nothing at all.

clue.text: General progressing initially at great speed

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
a ton is slang for 100 miles per hour, a great speed

explanation.surface: Things are, on the whole, moving along very quickly at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' reads as an adjective meaning overall but is the military rank. 'initially' takes the opening letter of 'progressing'. In British slang, doing a ton is travelling at 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: George S. Patton was an American army commander in the Second World War.

clue.text: Group taking holiday round centre of Sweden, stuck for accommodation

indicators.note: taking says the group word picks up the holiday word after it
round says the group word goes about the letters from Sweden

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians or of people

indicators.note: centre of asks for the middle two letters of the six in the word that follows

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
fast means firmly fixed, as in stuck fast

explanation.surface: A tour party travelling through the middle of Sweden cannot find anywhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the group word about ED, the middle of Sweden given by 'centre of'; 'taking' then adds the holiday word. 'stuck' is not part of the story but a word for fixed firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a guest house offering a room and a morning meal is one kind of lodging.

clue.text: Discover what makes night-time reading possible?

definitions.meaning: to come upon something by chance
a lamp that is switched to its working state lets you read after dark

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to chance upon, and a description of a lamp left burning at bedtime.

clue.text: Referee about to detain scrawny rugby player

indicators.note: to detain is to hold, so the turned referee word holds the scrawny word inside
about means turned round, so the referee word is written backwards

parts.note: lank means thin and scrawny

explanation.surface: A rugby official is on the point of holding back a skinny player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to' but turns REF into FER, and 'to detain' puts the scrawny word inside it. A flanker is a forward on the side of the rugby scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the forward positions in a rugby union team.

clue.text: Initially resuming, say, before tea's knocked back, I'll work my fingers to the bone?

definitions.text: I'll work my fingers to the bone?

indicators.note: knocked back sends the whole run of pieces into reverse order
before fixes the order of the pieces ahead of the turn, the tea coming last
Initially asks for the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
Assam is a tea from north-east India

explanation.surface: A worker going back on shift after a tea break complains about how hard the job is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests gulping the tea, but it turns the whole run of pieces round, with 'before' fixing their order first. 'Initially' takes the opening letter of 'resuming'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a masseur presses fingers into flesh right down towards the skeleton.

clue.text: Drive badly? Instruction provided

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street addresses
ill means badly, as in ill-treated or ill-prepared

explanation.surface: A poor motorist is given some lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' is not the verb here but the street name, as abbreviated on an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: repetitive training given to soldiers or pupils.

clue.text: Supporting Labour presumably used to be bizarre

parts.note: someone who backs Labour is presumably against the other main British party, and anti means against
the party a Labour supporter opposes is the Conservatives, abbreviated C

explanation.surface: Backing the Labour party was, one supposes, once thought very odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presumably' admits the whimsy: a backer of Britain's Labour party is taken to be against the Conservatives. 'used to be' marks the adjective sense as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adjective: in older English this word meant grotesque or fantastic.

clue.text: Dull theatre director's place?

parts.note: a director is in charge of the actors, so is placed above them
the actors a director is in charge of are the cast

explanation.surface: A rather boring spot is where the person running the play sits.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical description: where a director stands in the hierarchy, in two words, rather than a seat in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a grey, cloudy sky is a gloomy one.

clue.text: Note tennis player is losing, if this

definitions.meaning: to note something is to write it on paper

definitions.text: tennis player is losing, if this
definitions.meaning: a player who has lost the first of the match's sections is behind by one

explanation.definitionFit: To put in writing, and the state of a player trailing by one section of a match.

clue.text: Outcry as Indian language is introduced into school

indicators.note: is introduced into says the language is brought inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: Cree is a language of indigenous North Americans, once called Indians

explanation.surface: There are protests when a language from India is added to the school timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests India but means a native North American people. 'is introduced into' puts their language inside the abbreviation for school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a loud shrill cry or shriek.

clue.text: Innocent abroad in Calais, then Wales

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naive traveller visits a French port and then goes on to Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent abroad' reads as one phrase, a naive tourist, but splits: the first word is the definition and 'abroad' rearranges the letters of 'Calais', 'then' and 'Wales'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: said of someone with a spotless record, free of any guilt.

clue.text: Managed a domed structure

indicators.note: read as a command, structure means arrange or build, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was in charge of a building with a rounded roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'structure' looks like a noun for the building but is a verb telling you to rearrange the letters of 'a domed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coped or got by with what was available.

clue.text: Guard's pressure to join ranks again?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, leaving the verb guard as the definition

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to serve is to be in the forces, so to re-serve would be to enlist a second time

explanation.surface: A sentry feels pushed into signing up for the army once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' looks like a soldier but is a verb meaning protect. The question mark covers the invented verb re-serve, to do military service again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to keep safe from harm or protect.

clue.text: Little rock and roll, plus ballet only every now and then

indicators.note: plus adds the letters from ballet after the roll

parts.note: a cob is a round bread roll in British bakeries

indicators.note: only every now and then asks for every other letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A concert has a bit of rock and roll, with ballet only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock and roll' splits: 'Little rock' is a small stone and 'roll' is bread, a cob in Britain. 'only every now and then' takes the odd letters of 'ballet', BLE, and 'plus' adds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small rounded stone used for paving streets.

clue.text: Cross like elderly relative confined to home a short time

indicators.note: confined to says the first two pieces are shut inside the home and time pieces

parts.note: in means at home
T is the abbreviation, the short form, of time
to dig something is dated slang for to like it
nan is a British family word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy, like an old relation kept indoors for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is not a comparison but dated slang for enjoy, and the relative is a British word for grandmother. 'confined to' shuts both between the home word and the short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: angry at something felt to be unfair.

clue.text: Remedy reportedly associated with the States

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is heard when spoken rather than read

parts.note: linked means associated with, and the US is the States

explanation.surface: A cure is said to have American connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means a two-word phrase for 'associated with the States', linked US, is heard and respelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a syrupy medicine taken to soothe a cough.

clue.text: Pope's part in our banishment

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, leaving Pope as the definition

indicators.note: part in says the name is a stretch of letters within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The pontiff played a role in having us exiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' tells you the papal name runs across the join of 'our banishment'. Eight popes have used it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a name taken by eight pontiffs, the second of whom launched the First Crusade.

clue.text: Hard to deal with child in care after a week

indicators.note: after puts the child in care behind the other two pieces

parts.note: a ward is a child placed under a guardian's or court's care

explanation.surface: A fostered child becomes difficult to handle seven days into a placement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the word for a child in care behind A and the abbreviation for week.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tricky or difficult to handle.

clue.text: Dog wanting food runs inside

indicators.note: inside says the runs letter sits within the food word

parts.note: tack is an old word for food, as in a sailor's hard tack
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A hungry hound dashes into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb, to follow closely. 'inside' puts R, cricket's abbreviation for runs, into an old word for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to follow someone's trail closely.

clue.text: Talented people become less pale, climbing mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word before it is written upwards

parts.note: to tan is to grow browner in the sun
the Urals are the mountain range dividing Europe from Asia

explanation.surface: Gifted mountaineers get some colour in their cheeks as they ascend the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' seems to go with 'mountains' but belongs to the words before it: in a down clue it sends the word for getting browner upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: those with an inborn gift for something.

clue.text: Man has to pull out of show unavoidably

indicators.note: has to pull out of says the man must be withdrawn from the show word

parts.note: a performance is a show
taken as written

explanation.surface: A male actor is forced to withdraw from a production through no fault of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to pull out of' removes the letters MAN from inside an eleven-letter word for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal adverb meaning by necessity.

clue.text: My dog's nose twitches

indicators.note: twitches means jerks about, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the letters used as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet owner watches their dog's nose quiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is an exclamation of surprise. 'twitches' rearranges the letters of 'dog's nose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Examiner wearing glasses mostly to read at first

parts.note: someone wearing a coat is in it

indicators.note: mostly says the glasses word loses its final letter

parts.note: specs is the short form of spectacles
taken as written

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A marker puts on spectacles mainly in order to read the opening paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' is not a container signal here: it is a two-letter word, as in dressed in. 'mostly' drops the last letter of the glasses word and 'at first' takes the opening letter of 'read'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an official who checks or scrutinises things.

clue.text: Salad ingredient, so yummy — regularly better for starters

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it, and for starters says this piece comes first
sic is Latin for so or thus, used in quotations

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A diner says a tasty salad item is usually nicer as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb, to outdo, and 'for starters' sends it to the front. 'so' is its Latin form, and 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'yummy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet pepper often sliced raw into a mixed bowl of leaves.

clue.text: King Charles had head like this?

definitions.text: King Charles had head like this?

parts.words: King Charles had head like this?
parts.note: a monarch's head wears the regalia put on it at a coronation, and the same word is slang for struck on the head, a dark nod to Charles I's fate

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a monarch after the coronation ceremony, with a slang sense of a blow to the skull.

clue.text: Rogue appears to lack the heart for spicy meals

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a rogue

indicators.note: to lack the heart says the middle letter of the appears word is dropped

parts.note: the sun rises when it appears

explanation.surface: A scoundrel seems not to have the stomach for hot food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lack the heart' removes the central S from RISES, a word for appears, leaving RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: hot dishes of Indian cooking.

clue.text: How heavy smoker might cough and gag

definitions.meaning: damaged lungs make breathing and coughing come with a whistling rasp
British slang for a joke, trick or clever scheme

explanation.definitionFit: A rasping, whistling way of breathing, and British slang for a joke or prank.

clue.text: Woollen material is rather cute on daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the daughter letter

parts.note: twee means excessively sweet or cute
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A wool outfit looks quite sweet on someone's little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works literally in a down clue, standing the word for rather cute on top of the abbreviation for daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rough cloth woven in Scotland, used for jackets.

clue.text: Broadcaster initially hoping to avoiding downpour

indicators.note: avoiding says the downpour word goes without the letter just found

parts.note: a shower is a fall of rain

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A radio presenter at first hopes to stay out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' is not a presenter but someone scattering seed. 'initially' takes H from 'hoping', and 'to avoiding' drops it from the downpour word.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it by hand, which is what this farm worker does.
